lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies. Each man carries a trumpet, an empty jar, and a torch inside.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: Watch me, and do as I do. When I blow the trumpet, you blow yours and shout: For the Lord and for Gideon!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the start of the middle watch, the three companies blow their trumpets and break their jars. Torches blaze in left hands, trumpets in right.

lines.speaker: israelite_warrior
lines.text: A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every man stands in his place around the camp. The whole army runs, cries out, and flees. The Lord sets the Midianites' swords against one another.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The flight is captioned, not shown in injury. Israelites from the hill country join the pursuit. Ephraim captures Oreb and Zeeb — leaders, not kings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sequence settles. One coordinated action, staged in readable steps. The victory belonged to the Lord, not the three hundred.

choices.label: Hold the torch high
choices.note: The story keeps its shape; the cry carries the victory forward.

choices.label: Rest in the camp
choices.note: A pause does not change the outcome. It only lets the player breathe.
